title: Choosing collections
description:
Write these methods in `Text.java`, each with the collection that fits:

```java
class Text {
    static List<String> topWords(String text, int n)            // the n most frequent words, ties alphabetical
    static Character firstUnique(String s)                      // the first character that appears exactly once, or null
    static SortedMap<Integer, List<String>> byLength(List<String> words)   // lengths sorted; words in input order, no repeats
    static boolean isBalanced(String s)                         // brackets ( ) [ ] { } properly nested; other characters ignored
}
```

- Words in `topWords` are runs of letters, compared in lower case.
- `byLength(["fig", "pear", "kiwi", "fig", "plum"])` is `{3=[fig], 4=[pear, kiwi, plum]}`.
hints: A `LinkedHashMap` remembers insertion order, which is exactly "first" in `firstUnique`; a `TreeMap` keeps keys sorted, which suits `byLength`; a `LinkedHashSet` drops repeats but keeps order.

For `topWords`, count with a map, then put the words in a `TreeSet` so they are alphabetical. Go through the counts from the highest down to 1, and add the words with that count until you have `n`. (Lesson 4.03 shows a shorter way with a `Comparator`.)
For brackets, push each opening bracket on an `ArrayDeque` used as a stack; each closing bracket must match the one on top.
